lines.say: Your friend eats half a pizza. You eat half of what's left.
You didn't eat half a pizza. You ate half of a half. A quarter.

draw.alt: Pizza bar: half eaten by friend, then a quarter by you

lines.say: Every fraction is a fraction of something. Always ask: of what?
Mia has 90 dollars. She spends a third on a game and a quarter on food.
Both fractions are of the whole 90. So we can add them.
She has 5 twelfths left. 90 divided by 12, times 5, is 37.50.
Tom has 120 dollars. He spends a quarter on shoes. That's 30.

draw.alt: 120 dollar bar in four parts, shoes crossed off

lines.say: Then he spends two thirds of what is left on a jacket. Of the 90, not 120.

draw.alt: Two of the remaining three parts go on the jacket

lines.say: 90 minus 60 leaves 30 dollars.
Remainders multiply. 3 quarters left, then a third of that. A quarter.
If 3 fifths of a number is 24, one fifth is 24 divided by 3, which is 8.
The whole is 5 fifths. 8 times 5 is 40.
Ana spends 2 fifths, then half of what's left. She has 18 dollars.
lines.alt: Bar of 10 tenths: 4 spent, 3 spent, 3 left worth 18 dollars

lines.say: 3 fifths are left, then half of that. So 3 tenths is 18 dollars.
One tenth is 6 dollars. So she started with 60.
A tank is 3 eighths full. Add 45 litres and it's 3 quarters full.

draw.alt: Tank in eighths: 3 full, 3 more added by 45 litres

lines.say: The 45 litres is the change. 6 eighths minus 3 eighths is 3 eighths.
One eighth is 15 litres. The full tank is 15 times 8, which is 120.
Underline of what is left. Find the remainder first.
Only add fractions of the same whole.
Working backwards, the whole must be bigger than the part. Divide.
Of what? Point at each fraction and say.
Remainders multiply. Multiply the fractions that are left.
Part divided by fraction equals whole.
Draw the bar, then check forwards from your answer.
